title: My Beach Bag Packing List
text:
Tomorrow is Beach Day! My mom said I could pack my own bag this year, so I made a list.

Things to bring: sunscreen, so my nose does not get pink. A big striped towel. Two {adjective} buckets. A shovel for digging up {plural noun}. My lucky {noun}. Snacks: grapes, crackers, and a box of {food}.

Things my little brother wants to bring: his {adjective} dinosaur, exactly {number} {plural noun}, and a pet {animal}. Mom said no to all of them.

Dad is in charge of the umbrella. Last year he {past tense verb} while he was carrying it, and it flew away. This year he says he will hold it {adverb}.

I am so excited that I cannot stop {verb ending in ing}. I hope tomorrow is the most {adjective} day ever!

title: How to Build the Best Sandcastle
text:
Building a sandcastle is easy if you follow these steps. My big sister Rosie taught me, and she has won the Sandy Shores contest {number} times.

First, find a good spot. Not too close to the water, and not too close to the family with the {adjective} radio.

Next, fill your bucket with wet sand. Pat it down {adverb} and flip it over. Now you have a tower! Make three more and put a {noun} on top of each one.

Then dig a moat all the way around. Rosie says a good moat keeps out crabs, seagulls, and {plural noun}. Last year a seagull landed on her castle anyway and {past tense verb} on the tallest tower.

Now decorate. Use shells for windows and seaweed for the door. Rosie always adds a few {adjective} {plural noun} to make it fancy.

Last of all, stand back and admire your castle. If anyone asks who built it, put your hands on your hips and say "{silly word}!" Then go {verb ending in ing} into the waves to celebrate.

title: Lifeguard Larry's Beach Rules
text:
Hello, beach friends! I am Lifeguard Larry. I sit in the tall white chair and help everyone stay safe and happy. Please follow my beach rules.

Rule 1: Always swim with a grown-up nearby. Grown-ups are great at holding towels and {verb ending in ing}.

Rule 2: Do not feed the seagulls. They will follow you home and eat all of your {plural noun}.

Rule 3: Put on sunscreen every two hours. Do not forget the backs of your {plural noun}.

Rule 4: No digging holes bigger than a {noun}. Last week someone dug a hole so big that a family of {plural noun} moved in.

Rule 5: If you hear my whistle, please {verb} out of the water {adverb} and come see me. Usually it just means I found a {adjective} shell and want to show you.

Thank you for listening! Have a {adjective} day, and remember to always wear your {noun}.

title: Dad and the Runaway Umbrella
text:
Saturday. Today our family went to the beach. Dad carried a giant striped umbrella that he bought at a yard sale. He said it was the most {adjective} umbrella in the whole world.

First, Dad tried to stick it in the sand. It fell over. Then he tried again, and it {past tense verb} away. My little sister yelled "{exclamation}!" and we all chased it down the beach.

The umbrella rolled past a lady reading a book, two kids building a {noun}, and a dog named Biscuit. Biscuit started {verb ending in ing} and chased it too.

Finally the umbrella stopped next to a man selling {plural noun}. He helped Dad dig a hole {number} feet deep. Now the umbrella will never move again. We sat under it and ate sandwiches filled with {food}.

On the way home, Dad said next time we should {verb} instead. Mom laughed {adverb} and said she would bring a {adjective} tent.

title: Postcard from Seashell Beach
text:
Dear Grandma,

We are having the best time at Seashell Beach! The water is warm and the sand is as soft as a {noun}.

This morning I found {number} seashells and a {adjective} rock that looks just like a potato. I am bringing it home for you. Then I went swimming with my cousin Mia. We pretended we were {plural noun} and splashed {adverb} until lunch.

For lunch we had a picnic on our big blue blanket. A sneaky seagull took Mia's sandwich and flew away {verb ending in ing}. Mia was not even upset. She said the seagull looked very {adjective}.

Tonight we are going to watch the sunset and eat {food} by the fire. Dad says he will teach us to {verb} like a crab. I will practice so I can show you.

I miss you! Please give your cat a {adjective} hug from me.

Love,
Leo

title: Big News from the Sandcastle Contest
text:
Good afternoon! This is Sandy Waves with Beach News. I am standing on Pebble Beach at the yearly sandcastle contest.

This year {number} families came to build. The judges walked up and down the beach looking for the most {adjective} castle. One family built a castle shaped like a giant {noun}. Another family made a tower out of sand and {plural noun}. It was very tall and very {adjective}.

But the winner was seven-year-old Nora Lopez. Her castle had twelve rooms, a moat, and a little bridge made of {plural noun}. When the judges said her name, Nora {past tense verb} all the way to the prize table.

Nora won a gold trophy and a whole year of free {food}. We asked her for her secret. She said, "You have to {verb} {adverb} and never give up."

That's all from the beach. Back to you, and don't forget your {noun}!

title: Grandpa's Famous Beach Sandwiches
text:
Every time we go to the beach, Grandpa makes his famous beach sandwiches. He says they are the reason we always have the best day. Here is how he makes them.

You will need two slices of bread, one slice of cheese, a spoonful of {food}, a handful of {plural noun}, and a little bit of sand. The sand is always an accident.

First, wash your hands. Then lay the bread on a {adjective} plate. Put the cheese on top, then add the spoonful and the handful. Grandpa says to stir everything {adverb}, even though it is a sandwich. Next, squish the top slice down with your {body part}. Wrap it in a towel and put it in the cooler next to the {plural noun}.

At lunchtime, open the cooler and shout "{exclamation}!" That is what Grandpa always does. Then sit on the blanket and eat it while {verb ending in ing}.

Grandma says the sandwiches taste like a {adjective} {noun}. Last time, Grandpa said that meant she loved them, and he {past tense verb} with joy.

title: An Interview with Gary the Seagull
text:
Our class went to the beach for a field trip, and we got to interview a seagull named Gary.

Q: Hi, Gary! What do you do all day?
A: I fly around the beach and look for snacks. My favorite snack is {food}, but I will also eat {plural noun} if nobody is looking.

Q: Where do you live?
A: I live on top of the lifeguard chair. It is very {adjective} up there, and I can see everything.

Q: Do you have any hobbies?
A: Yes! I like to {verb} with my friends and collect shiny {plural noun}. I keep them in a {noun} under the pier.

Q: What is the hardest part of being a seagull?
A: The waves. Yesterday a big one splashed me, and I {past tense verb} for an hour.

Q: Do you have any advice for kids?
A: Always hold your sandwich {adverb}. And if you see a seagull {verb ending in ing}, give him a {adjective} wave.

Q: Thank you, Gary!
A: You are welcome. Now, are you going to finish those crackers?

title: Help Wanted: Ice Cream Cart Helper
text:
HELP WANTED at Mr. Pepper's Ice Cream Cart on Sunny Beach!

Mr. Pepper sells ice cream every summer. This year he has so many customers that he needs a helper. The right helper must be friendly, careful, and very {adjective}.

Your jobs will include scooping ice cream into cones, adding sprinkles and tiny {plural noun} on top, and ringing the bell {adverb} so people know we are here. You will also push the cart across the hot sand while {verb ending in ing}, and make sure the seagulls do not {verb} on the cart.

Our most popular flavor is strawberry. Our newest flavor is {food} swirl with chunks of {noun}. Last week a little boy tried it and {past tense verb} with joy.

The helper gets a free cone every day and a {color} hat with a pom-pom on top. If you would like the job, please come to the cart and sing {number} songs about {plural noun}.

title: Sunny Beach Lost and Found
text:
Attention, everyone at Sunny Beach! This is the snack shack with an important announcement.

Our Lost and Found box is full again. Today we found one flip-flop, three beach balls, and a {adjective} {noun}. If any of these are yours, please come get them before the sun goes down.

We also found a sand bucket full of {plural noun}. It was sitting next to the volleyball net and smelled a little bit like {food}.

And to the family who left their beach towel on the pier: a seagull is now sleeping on it {adverb}. He looks very {adjective}, so please {verb} quietly when you come to get it.

Finally, a little girl named Penny lost her favorite sun hat. It is bright pink with a picture of a {animal} on it. If you see it, please shout "{exclamation}!" and wave your {plural noun} in the air.

Thank you, and have a {adjective} day at the beach!
